candidates.exact_span: Based on the discharge frequency of the facility, the NMIP requires that pH has daily monitoring frequency and all other limited parameters have weekly monitoring frequency requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which parameters are 'limited' and the assigned daily vs. weekly monitoring frequencies affects Purpose B obligation rows; the same parameter classification bears on Purpose A distinctions between enforceable numeric limits and non-comparison monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: Flow is proposed to be monitored daily by estimate.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether flow monitoring is an enforceable numeric limit comparison or report-only/estimated monitoring depends on how 'proposed' daily-by-estimate flow is read, changing Purpose A limit-applicability rows and Purpose B monitoring-obligation applicability.

candidates.exact_span: The 48-hour WET testing for toxicity will be maintained for the proposed permit term. The frequency is 1/year. The CD of the discharge was previously determined to be 100%. The test species shall be Daphnia pulex.
candidates.computation_change_reason: WET test duration, annual frequency, critical dilution (100% CD), and species selection define the enforceable WET limit framework for Purpose A comparisons and the corresponding Purpose B monitoring schedule for Outfall 001.

candidates.exact_span: Because there was no data to analyze WET RP therefore conditions from the last permit will be carried over.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Carryover of prior-permit WET conditions when current RP data are absent affects which numeric WET limits apply under Purpose A and how Purpose C classifies the resulting no-data or inherited-limit evidence state.

candidates.exact_span: WET will be performed at first discharge.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A first-discharge trigger makes WET monitoring event-conditional rather than purely calendar-based; different readings of when 'first discharge' occurs or whether it happened in FY2025 change Purpose B applicability and Purpose C treatment of periods without WET results.

candidates.exact_span: During the period, beginning at the effective date of the permit and lasting through the expiration date of the permit, the permittee is authorized to discharge from Outfall 001 to the Corral Canyon.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The authorized discharge window and outfall/receiving-water scope bound which facilities, outfalls, and periods are in scope for Purpose A limit evaluation, Purpose B monitoring obligations, and Purpose C no-discharge vs. missing-evidence classification within Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Discharges are restricted to overflows from the retention pond due to catastrophic or chronic precipitation events.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Restricting discharges to overflow events under specified precipitation conditions affects whether discharge occurred in a monitoring period (Purpose B event-conditioned requirements) and whether absent measurements reflect documented no-discharge periods versus missing required evidence (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: Discharges of storm water runoff from access roads in undisturbed areas shall be covered under the NPDES Multi-Sector Storm Water Permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Routing access-road stormwater to a separate multi-sector permit can exclude those flows from Outfall 001 numeric limits and monitoring under this permit, changing Purpose A limit scope and Purpose B obligation rows for road-runoff parameters.

candidates.exact_span: If a discharge of storm runoffs from mining areas is necessary, the discharge must comply with effluent limitations established at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Conditional applicability of Outfall 001 effluent limitations to mining-area storm runoff affects which numeric limits govern those flows under Purpose A and whether monitoring for them is required only when discharge is 'necessary' under Purpose B and Purpose C.

candidates.exact_span: The applicant is required to operate the treatment facility at maximum efficiency at all times; to monitor the facility's discharge on a regular basis; and report the results quarterly.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The unspecified 'regular basis' monitoring coupled with quarterly reporting could be read as distinct from the NMIP-derived daily/weekly frequencies, affecting which monitoring intervals are actually required in Purpose B rows for FY2025.
